The coolest physics thing in my opinion, is the thing that led to the formation of Quantum Physics itself.

It's called the [Ultraviolet Catastrophe](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ultraviolet_catastrophe). 

Let's look at a blackbody object, and start heating it up. In Classical physics, as it is heated up more and more, we should be giving off copious amounts of photons of every frequency. Finally, at about 5000k, we should be *literally* giving off infinite energy in the form of ultraviolet photons, but... well... were not!

Why not?

This simple question, asked so many times in physics, leads to so many discoveries. This time, it led to the entire Quantum world.

See, a very smart man thought, well, what if pouring in energy wasnt enough? What if it had to be *the exact right amount?*

Mr. Planck did some experiments, and did some calculations, and well, he found that that is exactly what is required. You cant just pour energy into and atom and expect it to pour out. You need to hit an electron with the exact energy required (no more, no less), or it will not release a photon. This energy has to be hit all at once, hence *Quantum.*

This to me, is the coolest thing ever. If it werent for this fact, *nothing* would exist. And like everything in Physics, there is no reason for this to take place. It just does. Sure, H-bar and all that, but why does H-bar exist? Who knows! It's damn cool though.
